newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia peso closes up after holiday break.
newsitem.headline: Colombia peso closes up after holiday break.

text.p: Colombia's peso gained two pesos to end at 998.2 to the dollar, its highest closing rate since early January, interbank traders said.

Returning after Monday's national holiday, dealers said the peso closed above the 1,000 to the dollar psychological barrier on the back of industry pumping its dollar export earnings into the market and a wave of speculative currency trading by banks.

"There was bit of everything in the session today. Dollar export earnings from oil were being pumped into the market at the same time as dollars from foreign loans being traded for pesos," one dealer said.
Some banks were selling greenbacks high and rebuying as the dollar rate dropped as dealers reported trades worth a total $95.5 million.
The peso hit an intraday high of 997.5 to the dollar and an intraday low of 1,000.4. There were no reports of central bank intervention to prop up the dollar.
